kind: Your streak in view, a reading room on a stage, and every quotation with its source
blurb: Purify 1.7.1 brings much of what you asked for since 1.7. Your streak sits at the top of every tab. The reading room opens on a stage for the day's book, with rows for how you feel. You is rebuilt around what you keep, highlights come in six colours you can name, and the people you pray for, from your family to the prayer wall, now stand inside your prayers. Every quotation says where it comes from and opens there, and the calendar is made for your phone.
items: Your streak, in view. A flame and your count sit beside Premium at the top of every tab, and a tap opens your streak. The flame grows as you keep it: Spark from the first day, Candle at seven, Lamp at forty, Crown at a hundred, and All flame at a year, after Abba Joseph's saying in the Sayings of the Desert Fathers.

The reading room, on a stage. The day's book stands at the top on its own picture, and the room settles in as you scroll. Short reads come first, and New to Orthodoxy comes first if you are new. A row for how you feel opens eight Purify collections (love, anger, hatred, fear and worry, grief, despondency, envy and loneliness): 79 passages of Scripture and the Fathers, word for word, each opening where it stands.

Those I pray for. Your living and your departed, and the names you add from the prayer wall, now stand in one list inside your prayers, in the prayers you choose: morning, midday, evening, the Hours, Compline or your own rule. When you ask for prayers on the wall, you can say what to pray for, and it goes with your name into the prayers of everyone who adds you.

Every quotation says where it comes from. A saint's words, a Father's comment on a chapter, a council or a line of Scripture carries its exact place, and a tap opens it there, down to the paragraph. Lines we could not trace to a public-domain text have left the page, and the Fathers' books are cited by their own numbering.

You, rebuilt. Pick up where you left off, meet a verse you kept each day to read in its chapter, learn by heart or share, and find everything you have kept, sorted into verses, writings, saints, prayers, readings and icons.

The calendar, made for your phone. The month fits the screen, and the arrows or a swipe turn it. The day you choose sits below: its fast, its saints with their icons, and its readings, each one opening the Bible. New and Old Calendar is one switch, and Today is one tap.

items.text: St Augustine's Confessions, all thirteen books, word for word, with its books, chapters and sections numbered as the Latin numbers them.
The reading room's covers are posters now. The picture fills the cover, the title sits on it, and no title is cut short at any size. A book with no picture has a poster of its own.
Highlights come in six colours of Purify's own, picked with one thumb, and you can name what each colour means. Saved sorts your highlights by colour, and a Father's books take the same colours.
Learn to Pray shows the Sign of the Cross with a real hand, three fingers joined and two folded, and traces the four touches in their order as it comes into view.
On John 1, the reading bar has a play button that reads the chapter aloud.
Today's saying comes from the Desert Fathers, word for word from the library, with its place.
The walkthrough of Job says who each person is to the Church: their icon, their title and their feast.
The Verse of the Day in Turkish: a machine translation from the English, marked as one where you read it, until Purify has a Turkish Bible.
Remember the verse says what it is, sets out each word's first letter, and lets you check yourself a word at a time or the whole verse at once.
Icons are cut clean, with no white at their edges: ten saints, four prayer icons and four pictures in Orthodox History. The Pantocrator in Start here now comes close to His face.
Search in the Bible opens on a screen of its own, above everything else, and its results stop where your keyboard begins.
Holding on the words no longer covers the reading bar. The bar steps aside while Copy is up, and comes back after.
Chants stay where they are while Purify checks which recordings can play, and say plainly why one cannot: no connection, or not available right now.
Covers and the saints' pictures arrive calmly instead of popping in, and a picture that does not load is tried once more.
Pray with chant has a clearer play button, and a check marks the chant you chose.
On iPad, the Bible and a Father's writings sit in the middle of the screen, and Orthodox History's parts land where you tap.
On an Android tablet or an unfolded foldable, Purify now turns with the screen. Phones stay upright.
The calendar's marks for feasts and for wine and oil are easier to tell apart, and a saint's repose reads "† ca. 290" where it showed a plus.
The calendar keeps your place when you tap a day, and its readings are set in the app's own type.
